title: Date set for inquest into death of woman in holding cell at Niagara police headquarters
subtitle: Sabrina Van Vessem, 24, suffered a fatal overdose in 2020 while being held in custody by Niagara Regional Police.
article: A date has been set for an inquest into the death of a 24-year-old woman who suffered an overdose while in Niagara police custody in 2020.

In a news release issued Friday afternoon, Dr. Karen Schiff, regional supervising coroner for West Region's Hamilton office, announced the inquest into the death of Sabrina Van Vessem will begin at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, Feb. 3.
The presiding officer will be Dr. Geoffrey Bond, while Jai Dhar will be the inquest counsel.
Van Vessem died on May 21, 2020, while in custody at Niagara Regional Police headquarters in Niagara Falls.
The release noted an inquest examining circumstances surrounding the death is mandatory under the provincial Coroners Act and could lead to recommendations to prevent further deaths.
In a May 2020 release, the province's Special Investigations Unit said the woman died of a drug overdose in her cell.
She had been arrested shortly after 5 p.m. the day before, on May 20, in the area of Kitchener Street and Slater Avenue in Niagara Falls for breaching court conditions.
On the day she died, she attended a tele-bail hearing at about 2 p.m. and was returned to her cell.
he was found unresponsive just before 5 p.m. Niagara Emergency Medical Services was called, and the woman was pronounced dead.
In 2021, the SIU said it had concluded there was no basis for proceeding with criminal charges against the officer in charge of the station at the time of her death.
However, the SIU said police missed mandated well-being checks of the prisoner in her cell every 30 minutes.

The inquest is expected to last five days and will hear from about nine witnesses. It will be conducted by video conference, which will be available to the public at firstclassfacilitation.ca/office-of-the-chief-coroner/inquest-into-the-death-of-Sabrina-Van-Vessem/.
